summary: Following the GBC Joint Statement, the Thai military (Army Regions 1 and 2) reported successful reclamation and control of key strategic border areas. In Sa Kaeo, Thai forces secured Ban Khlong Phaeng, Ban Nong Chan, and Ban Nong Ya Kaeo. In Surin and Sisaket, troops established control over Hill 225 and areas near Preah Vihear before the 12:00 PM ceasefire took effect on Dec 27. The 72-hour window is now being used to verify sincerity before the potential return of 18 captured Cambodian soldiers.
summaryEn: Following the GBC Joint Statement, the Thai military (Army Regions 1 and 2) reported successful reclamation and control of key strategic border areas. In Sa Kaeo, Thai forces secured Ban Khlong Phaeng, Ban Nong Chan, and Ban Nong Ya Kaeo. In Surin and Sisaket, troops established control over Hill 225 and areas near Preah Vihear before the 12:00 PM ceasefire took effect on Dec 27. The 72-hour window is now being used to verify sincerity before the potential return of 18 captured Cambodian soldiers.

summary: The Election Commission (EC) of Thailand has published special guidelines in the Royal Gazette to ensure the upcoming general election can proceed in Chanthaburi, Trat, Buri Ram, Si Sa Ket, Sa Kaeo, Surin, and Ubon Ratchathani. Due to the border conflict and evacuations, officials are authorized to use electronic systems for voter list notifications if physical delivery is unsafe, and to adapt polling procedures to prioritize voter safety without disenfranchising citizens in conflict zones.
summaryEn: The Election Commission (EC) of Thailand has published special guidelines in the Royal Gazette to ensure the upcoming general election can proceed in Chanthaburi, Trat, Buri Ram, Si Sa Ket, Sa Kaeo, Surin, and Ubon Ratchathani. Due to the border conflict and evacuations, officials are authorized to use electronic systems for voter list notifications if physical delivery is unsafe, and to adapt polling procedures to prioritize voter safety without disenfranchising citizens in conflict zones.

summary: Thai and Cambodian General Border Committee (GBC) secretariats have finalized a draft ceasefire agreement after three days of tense negotiations in Chanthaburi. The deal, which includes a 72-hour halt to hostilities, is scheduled for signing by the defense ministers of both nations on Saturday, Dec 27. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated that Thailand will not trade territory for business interests and that the military has successfully established sovereignty over contested areas.
summaryEn: Thai and Cambodian General Border Committee (GBC) secretariats have finalized a draft ceasefire agreement after three days of tense negotiations in Chanthaburi. The deal, which includes a 72-hour halt to hostilities, is scheduled for signing by the defense ministers of both nations on Saturday, Dec 27. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated that Thailand will not trade territory for business interests and that the military has successfully established sovereignty over contested areas.

summary: The Second Army Region of Thailand reports that it has successfully gained 100% control over the Ban Nong Chan area. summary: Details of the 3rd Special General Border Committee (GBC) meeting report a 16-point agreement. Key points include an immediate ceasefire starting at 12:00 PM on Dec 27 covering all weapons, freezing troop movements/patrols, and allowing civilians to return home. The agreement explicitly states it does not affect border demarcation, which remains the responsibility of the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC).

summary: Thai and Cambodian defense ministers signed a Joint Statement in Chanthaburi to end hostilities. summary: Thailand and Cambodia signed a 16-point Joint Statement during the General Border Committee (GBC) meeting, effective Dec 27, 2025, at 12:00 PM. The agreement mandates an immediate halt to all weapon use and troop movements. Both sides must maintain current positions without advancement or provocation. A 72-hour monitoring period is established to verify compliance. Following this period, Thailand will return 18 captured Cambodian soldiers.

The agreement mandates an immediate halt to all weapon use and troop movements. Both sides must maintain current positions without advancement or provocation. A 72-hour monitoring period is established to verify compliance. Following this period, Thailand will return 18 captured Cambodian soldiers.
summaryKh: ថៃនិងកម្ពុជាបានចុះហត្ថលេខាលើសេចក្តីថ្លែងការណ៍រួម 16 ចំណុចក្នុងកិច្ចប្រជុំ GBC ដែលមានប្រសិទ្ធភាពចាប់ពីម៉ោង 12 ថ្ងៃត្រង់ ថ្ងៃទី 27 ធ្នូ 2025។ កិច្ចព្រមព្រៀងនេះតម្រូវឱ្យបញ្ឈប់ការបាញ់គ្នាភ្លាមៗ និងហាមឃាត់ការចល័តទ័ព។ ភាគីទាំងពីរត្រូវរក្សាតំណែងបច្ចុប្បន្នដោយមិនមានការរំកិលទៅមុខឬការញុះញង់ឡើយ។ នឹងមានការតាមដានរយៈពេល 72 ម៉ោង ហើយបន្ទាប់មកថៃនឹងប្រគល់ទាហានកម្ពុជា 18 នាក់ត្រឡប់ទៅវិញ។

summary: The General Border Committee (GBC) released a 16-point joint statement signed by the defense ministers of Thailand and Cambodia. Key measures include an immediate ceasefire effective Dec 27 at noon, a ban on moving additional troops or provocative actions, and a commitment to humanitarian landmine clearance. The agreement also includes a clause to refrain from disseminating fake news about the conflict.

Just before the noon deadline, one Thai soldier was reported severely injured by a newly planted landmine.

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) acknowledged the ceasefire agreement reached at the 3rd Special GBC meeting held at Ban Phakkad, Chanthaburi. Thailand set three clear conditions for the truce: 1) Official and sincere declaration, 2) Actual and continuous cessation of fighting, and 3) Sincerity in resolving landmine issues. The MFA expressed condolences for the brave Thai soldiers who sacrificed their lives protecting sovereignty. The 72-hour observation window will determine if civilians can safely return home.
summaryEn: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) acknowledged the ceasefire agreement reached at the 3rd Special GBC meeting held at Ban Phakkad, Chanthaburi. Thailand set three clear conditions for the truce: 1) Official and sincere declaration, 2) Actual and continuous cessation of fighting, and 3) Sincerity in resolving landmine issues. The MFA expressed condolences for the brave Thai soldiers who sacrificed their lives protecting sovereignty. The 72-hour observation window will determine if civilians can safely return home.

summary: The Thai Mine Action Centre (TMAC) has condemned Cambodia for laying fresh PMN-2 landmines along the border in Si Sa Ket province. This follows an incident where a Thai soldier lost his leg. TMAC claims to have found evidence, including a GPS notepad left by retreating Cambodian forces, indicating the mines were recently placed, violating the Ottawa Convention.
summaryKh: មជ្ឈមណ្ឌលសកម្មភាពកំចាត់មីនថៃ (TMAC) បានថ្កោលទោសកម្ពុជា ចំពោះការដាក់គ្រាប់មីន PMN-2 ថ្មីតាមព្រំដែនក្នុងខេត្តស៊ីសាកេត។ នេះកើតឡើងបន្ទាប់ពីមានហេតុការណ៍ទាហានថៃម្នាក់បានដាច់ជើងដោយសារជាន់មីន។ TMAC អះអាងថាបានរកឃើញភស្តុតាង រួមទាំងសៀវភៅកត់ត្រា GPS ដែលបន្សល់ទុកដោយកងកម្លាំងកម្ពុជាដែលដកថយ ដែលបង្ហាញថាគ្រាប់មីនទាំងនោះត្រូវបានដាក់ថ្មីៗនេះ។
summaryTh: ศูนย์ปฏิบัติการทุ่นระเบิดแห่งชาติ (TMAC) ประณามกัมพูชาที่ลอบวางทุ่นระเบิด PMN-2 ใหม่ตามแนวชายแดนในจังหวัดศรีสะเกษ หลังเกิดเหตุทหารไทยเหยียบระเบิดจนเสียขา โดย TMAC อ้างว่าพบหลักฐานรวมถึงสมุดจดพิกัด GPS ที่กองกำลังกัมพูชาทิ้งไว้ขณะถอยร่น ซึ่งชี้ชัดว่าเป็นทุ่นระเบิดที่เพิ่งวางใหม่ อันเป็นการละเมิดอนุสัญญาออตตาวา

summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio released a statement through the US Embassy in Bangkok welcoming the ceasefire between Thailand and Cambodia following the GBC meeting. He urged both nations to strictly adhere to the 'Kuala Lumpur Peace Accords.' Meanwhile, Thai Caretaker PM Anutin Charnvirakul is scheduled to visit Buriram to oversee the safe return of displaced villagers to their homes following the cessation of hostilities.

summary: Prime Minister and Interior Minister Anutin Charnvirakul is traveling to Buriram to oversee the return of displaced persons from shelters to their homes. This follows the 72-hour ceasefire window established during GBC talks. Anutin noted the situation is improving but remained skeptical of reports regarding Belarusian transport planes landing in Phnom Penh, stating security agencies are monitoring the situation closely.

summary: Air Chief Marshal Prapas Sornjaidee, spokesperson for the joint situation center, stated that the military remains on high alert. summary: Acting PM Anutin Charnvirakul discussed the outcome of the GBC meeting, stating the Joint Statement clearly binds both nations to cease hostilities. summaryTh: นายอนุทิน ชาญวีรกูล รองนายกฯ ระบุว่าแถลงการณ์ร่วม (Joint Statement) จากการประชุม GBC มีความชัดเจนว่าทั้งสองฝ่ายจะไม่ละเมิดกันอีก โดยหวังว่ากัมพูชาจะรักษาสัญญา พร้อมระบุว่าฝ่ายความมั่นคงกำลังตรวจสอบข่าวลือเรื่องเครื่องบินเบลารุสขนอาวุธไปพนมเปญ นอกจากนี้จีนยังได้เชิญ รมว.ต่างประเทศทั้งสองฝ่ายไปหารือสันติภาพเพิ่มเติมที่คุนหมิงวันที่ 28-29 ธ.ค. นี้

summary: Reports from Cambodia's Customs Department show a 35% decrease in imports from Thailand between June and November 2025 due to border tensions and the closure of key trade checkpoints like Sai Taku and Chong Jom. summary: Army Region 2 reported that overall tensions have eased following the midday ceasefire on December 27. summary: ACM Prapas Sonjaidee, director of Thailand's Joint Press Centre, stated that Thailand now expects diplomatic forums to resolve differences instead of the battlefield. While the truce is holding and evacuees are returning, the Thai Air Force monitored a Russian-built IL-62 aircraft from Belarus landing in Phnom Penh. Thailand maintains its right to self-defense and retaliation if weapons are used again, while documenting evidence for international organizations.

summary: Caretaker PM Anutin Charnvirakul disclosed that China has offered 20 million yuan (approx. 95 million THB) in aid to both Thailand and Cambodia for post-conflict reconstruction. Anutin visited border provinces including Buriram and Surin to oversee the return of displaced persons. He noted that while social media questioned China's neutrality, the offer was extended to both nations. He also visited strategic sites like Prasat Ta Kwai to boost morale.

summary: Bilateral trade between Thailand and Cambodia has taken a severe hit due to border tensions. Data from Cambodia's Customs Department shows a 34.5% decrease in imports from Thailand in the second half of 2025, falling from $1.77 billion to $1.25 billion. The drop is attributed to the closure of key border crossings like Sai Taku and Chong Jom during the height of the conflict.

summary: The Thailand Mine Action Centre (TMAC) discovered PMN-2 anti-personnel landmines at abandoned Cambodian bases in Si Sa Ket, along with logs of mine-laying operations. A Thai soldier lost a leg after stepping on a mine shortly after the ceasefire began. Additionally, BM-21 rocket remnants were found in Buriram farmlands. TMAC urged Cambodia to disclose mine locations to ensure safety.

summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow met with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Cambodian FM Prak Sokhonn in Yunnan. summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow met with Cambodian FM Prak Sokhonn and Chinese FM Wang Yi in Yunnan. China emphasized it respects the principle of non-interference but wishes to facilitate a channel for both countries to discuss lasting peace. summary: The Royal Thai Army (RTA) announced on December 29 that it detected over 250 Cambodian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) violating Thai sovereignty. This activity is considered a breach of the GBC de-escalation agreement. As a result, the RTA is reconsidering the release of 18 Cambodian soldiers who were to be repatriated after a successful 72-hour ceasefire. The Army emphasized its duty to protect national interests while remaining committed to peace mechanisms.

As a result, the RTA is reconsidering the release of 18 Cambodian soldiers who were to be repatriated after a successful 72-hour ceasefire. The Army emphasized its duty to protect national interests while remaining committed to peace mechanisms.

summary: The Thai Army reported detecting numerous Cambodian drones violating Thai airspace, totaling over 250 incursions. Consequently, the planned release of 18 Cambodian prisoners of war, originally scheduled for noon on December 30 after a 72-hour ceasefire, has been postponed. The Thai military views these drone activities as a violation of the de-escalation measures agreed upon during the recent GBC meeting.

Consequently, the planned release of 18 Cambodian prisoners of war, originally scheduled for noon on December 30 after a 72-hour ceasefire, has been postponed. The Thai military views these drone activities as a violation of the de-escalation measures agreed upon during the recent GBC meeting.

summary: In the wake of a brokered ceasefire, China hosted trilateral talks in Yunnan province on December 29. While Beijing positions itself as a peacemaker, tension remains as the Thai army reports drone violations by Cambodia. Thailand is reportedly 'reconsidering' the planned release of 18 Cambodian prisoners due to these fresh violations of the ceasefire agreement.
summaryEn: In the wake of a brokered ceasefire, China hosted trilateral talks in Yunnan province on December 29. While Beijing positions itself as a peacemaker, tension remains as the Thai army reports drone violations by Cambodia. Thailand is reportedly 'reconsidering' the planned release of 18 Cambodian prisoners due to these fresh violations of the ceasefire agreement.

summary: Local reporters in Surin noted that residents who returned home during the 72-hour ceasefire (expiring noon, Dec 30) are on high alert. Cambodian sources claimed their military has not allowed Cambodian civilians back into the O'Smach area, contrasting with Thai authorities allowing Thais to return. Vendors at Chong Chom market expressed a lack of trust in the ceasefire and readiness to flee immediately if fighting erupts.

Vendors at Chong Chom market expressed a lack of trust in the ceasefire and readiness to flee immediately if fighting erupts.

summary: Thailand has officially postponed the scheduled release of 18 Cambodian soldiers (originally set for Dec 30) after security agencies detected Cambodian drones violating Thai airspace. This action is considered a breach of the GBC joint statement which prohibits provocations. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Nikorndej Balankura stated the landmine incidents are also a serious concern for the Thai side.
summaryEn: Thailand has officially postponed the scheduled release of 18 Cambodian soldiers (originally set for Dec 30) after security agencies detected Cambodian drones violating Thai airspace. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Nikorndej Balankura stated the landmine incidents are also a serious concern for the Thai side.

summary: The National Mine Action Center (NMAC) reported that on Dec 29, a Thai soldier from the 1st Cavalry Division lost his left leg and suffered eye injuries after stepping on a landmine while clearing an area in Kantharalak, Sisaket. This is the 11th Thai soldier to suffer such a loss since the conflict began. NMAC condemned the use of mines as a violation of the Ottawa Convention.

Thailand has established a 'Red Line' (prohibiting sovereignty violation, civilian attacks, or threats). Responses will be proportionate to the level of provocation. Decisions on the 18 prisoners depend on humanitarian and safety assessments.

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs officially confirmed the repatriation of 18 Cambodian soldiers who had been held since July 2025. The release occurred at 10:00 AM on December 31, 2025, following a 72-hour ceasefire. The ministry emphasized that the soldiers were treated in accordance with the 1949 Geneva Convention and international humanitarian laws. The ICRC and ASEAN Observation Team (AOT) witnessed the handover, which Thailand hopes will build trust and lead to lasting peace.
summaryEn: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs officially confirmed the repatriation of 18 Cambodian soldiers who had been held since July 2025. The release occurred at 10:00 AM on December 31, 2025, following a 72-hour ceasefire. The ministry emphasized that the soldiers were treated in accordance with the 1949 Geneva Convention and international humanitarian laws. The ICRC and ASEAN Observation Team (AOT) witnessed the handover, which Thailand hopes will build trust and lead to lasting peace.

summaryTh: กองทัพภาคที่ 2 รายงานว่าสถานการณ์อยู่ภายใต้การควบคุม ไม่มีการปะทะด้วยอาวุธหนักหลังพ้นกำหนดหยุดยิง 72 ชั่วโมง อย่างไรก็ตาม พบโดรนกัมพูชาบินลาดตระเวนใกล้ปราสาทตาควาย และยังคงมีการเสริมกำลังทหารใกล้เขาพระวิหาร
